title: CLO 2024 Course  Summer Essential! CLO Teaches You How to Make 3D Fashion Sun-Protective Clothing!
description:
In the scorching summer heat, learn how to make an essential summer item—the 3D sun-protection jacket—with CLO!  
CLO technical expert Lydia will guide you through the entire process, from modifying a basic jacket pattern to the final product presentation, while enhancing your design with PBR textures and preset mapping features!  
Start learning now and stay cool this summer with CLO!  
For free materials from this livestream, please reply “Free Materials” in the CLO3D official WeChat account.

chunks.title: CLO 2024 Course  Summer Essential! CLO Teaches You How to Make 3D Fashion Sun-Protective Clothing!
chunks.content: # CLO 2024 Course: Making 3D Sun-Protective Fashion Clothing This document details the step-by-step process, features, and technical instructions for creating a 3D sun-protective clothing suit using CLO 2024.1 software. It covers pattern modification, garment detailing, new 3D tools, fabric transparency effects, sewing techniques, sticker generation, and rendering settings. --- ## Overview of the 3D Sunscreen Suit Project This section introduces the workflow for designing a 3D sun-protective clothing suit using CLO 2024.1. Key concepts include pattern modification, garment detailing (elastic bands, pleats, zippers), and leveraging new 3D features like automatic 3D stickers and enhanced garment simulation with green color effects. --- ## Preparing Virtual Model and Clothing Files - Use the official Kinect female model without a face for simplicity; this virtual model includes built-in sunscreen suit information. - Open the clothing file downloaded from the official CLO account. - Both model and garment display transparent effects. - Use **Automatic Wear** function to dress the model quickly. This function adapts the clothing to the model’s sunscreen suit data, ensuring correct positioning and fit on various models. --- ## Organizing and Modifying 2D Patterns - Clean the workspace by deleting unnecessary panels (e.g., storage panel, middle panel). - Arrange 2D panels logically: front panel at the model’s shadow, sleeves on either side, and back panel adjacent. - Use the **Hook Wheel Tool** (shortcut: I) to cut and remove unnecessary inner lines and panels. - Merge pattern pieces after cleanup to create a base sample. - Confirm the base sample before proceeding with modifications. --- ## Using Column Reference Lines for Pattern Adjustment - Set a pattern version as a **Column Reference Line** to compare before-and-after modifications. - Use the **Adjustment Version Tool** to edit patterns while referencing the original. - Revert changes easily by selecting edges and pressing return key to reconnect to the reference line. - Modify patterns in both 2D and 3D views for precise adjustments. --- ## Adding and Adjusting Zippers in 3D - Add zippers using the **Zipper Function** directly in 3D. - Use the **Shape Line Tool** to adjust garment dimensions; subtypes include: - Edit Shape Line - Zipper Shape Line - Mobile Shape Line - Configuration Shape Line - To shorten or change zipper length, activate the **Zipper Shape Line**, select the dimension, and adjust by dragging or entering exact values. - Simulate changes in 3D for real-time visualization. --- ## Joint Editing Function for Seam Lines - Delete intermediate sewing lines on side seams to create a continuous seam. - Use the **Edit Sewing Line Tool**, right-click and select **Joint Line** to connect sewing lines. - A small arrow icon appears on joint lines indicating they are linked. - Multi-line selection lets you adjust connected seams simultaneously. - Use **Ctrl key** to control joint line direction and angle (aim for ~90 degrees per joint for a 180-degree combined angle). - Simulate to verify seam accuracy and garment fit after edits.

chunks.content: --- ## Joint Editing Function for Seam Lines - Delete intermediate sewing lines on side seams to create a continuous seam. - Use the **Edit Sewing Line Tool**, right-click and select **Joint Line** to connect sewing lines. - A small arrow icon appears on joint lines indicating they are linked. - Multi-line selection lets you adjust connected seams simultaneously. - Use **Ctrl key** to control joint line direction and angle (aim for ~90 degrees per joint for a 180-degree combined angle). - Simulate to verify seam accuracy and garment fit after edits. --- ## Sleeve Modification and Thumb Movement Design - Change sleeve lines to straight by deleting middle curve points. - Add cutout points using the **Cutout Tool** (right-click). - Adjust line lengths with the **Change Length Tool**, applying changes symmetrically to both sides. - Pull sleeve downwards carefully without twisting to maintain fit. - Use **Semi-Transparent Display** (shortcut 2+4) in 3D to inspect wrist and seam positions. - Create internal multilayer lines near key points and apply tight seams for thumb movement allowance. - Cut off unnecessary pattern plates (e.g., Shoukofu plate) using vertical internal line tools and delete unwanted internal lines or Shoukofu lines. - Finalize sleeve by sewing edges, adjusting seam lines, widening bottom circumference, and adding thumb hole designs with free sewing. --- ## Loose Belt Design and Assembly - Loose belt length is 590 mm. - Use the **Calculator Function** to apply tightening: multiply length by 0.8 to achieve 80% tightening. - Use symmetrical edit sewing line to ensure uniform assembly. - Create a two-centimeter internal line before sewing. - Use the new **Hook and Loop Sewing Line Type** introduced in 2024.1 (shortcut next to wheelbarrow key) to replace previous fold selections. - Sew seams ensuring board outside lines overlap. - Simulate to check fit and function. --- ## Sun Visor (Hat) Construction - Design an extended board for better coverage on the sun visor. - Add and adjust points and curves carefully to shape the visor. - Measure hat edge width (e.g., 293 mm) and create rough pocket shapes using curve tools. - Rotate and align boards referencing original shapes. - Use internal line display for precision. - Delete unnecessary sewing lines and add relevant boards to the outside. - Complete the visor by sewing along designed lines. --- ## Applying Fabric Materials and Transparency Effects - Apply fabric textures from flour files; the sunscreen fabric is thin and semi-transparent. - Adjust fabric opacity to approximately 70-75% for realistic transparency. - Use high-quality rendering filters to check transparency effects. - Apply blurring to simulate realistic fabric transparency (less transparent than 3D window preview). - Replace original textures and hairlines with custom images. - CLO 2024.1 introduces **Automatic PBR Sticker Generation** for hair lines, gaze patterns, and surface saturation textures. - Adjust strength values (e.g., 60 degrees) for desired effect intensity. --- ## Creating Double-Sided Fabric Layers and Drawstring Patterns - For transparent fabrics, bottom and inner layers must be double-sided.

chunks.content: - Use high-quality rendering filters to check transparency effects. - Apply blurring to simulate realistic fabric transparency (less transparent than 3D window preview). - Replace original textures and hairlines with custom images. - CLO 2024.1 introduces **Automatic PBR Sticker Generation** for hair lines, gaze patterns, and surface saturation textures. - Adjust strength values (e.g., 60 degrees) for desired effect intensity. --- ## Creating Double-Sided Fabric Layers and Drawstring Patterns - For transparent fabrics, bottom and inner layers must be double-sided. - Create double-layered drawstring patches at inner seams and collar positions. - Use the **Hook and Loop Tool** to set hemline positions and close hook-and-loop patterns. - Apply symmetry and change outer lines to fold sewing line type using shortcuts. - Add panels inside and sew all necessary seams. - Simulate often to ensure fit and appearance. --- ## Door and Pocket Pattern Details - Measure and create straight and curve lines to fit the sewing positions of doors and pockets. - Adjust heights and shapes to align with overall garment design. - Rotate and flip boards as necessary. - Use edit circle and board adjustment tools to refine curves and alignments. - Sew lines using line sewing tool and check length accuracy (e.g., 569.8 mm reference). - Use stickers for seam details to enhance realism. --- ## Sewing Wrinkles and Puller Details - Add puller details at neckline and loose belt areas using the **Puller Tool**. - Default puller height is 4 cm; position pullers at desired locations. - Use the **Sewing Wrinkles Tool** to add realistic wrinkle effects with shape lines. - Edit material type to nylon for more detailed sewing effects. - Adjust wrinkle width and strength for desired delicacy. - Wrinkles affect appearance only, not garment simulation. - Add internal multidirectional lines on inner layers with 1 mm width. - Before simulation, adjust puller positions in 3D by placing positioning balls and rotating/moving to avoid interference. - Use color adjustment to refine puller texture visibility. --- ## Sticker Creation and Effects - Use stickers from the material document holder and drag onto garments. - Adjust sticker position in both 2D and 3D. - Auto-generate stickers with built-in editor; modify colors and picture effects. - Use **Effect Presets** in the attribute editor with options such as Default, Array Effect (crack-like), Retrofine, and Gold. - Gold preset can be adjusted to silver or light gray. - Adjust height map using **Change-Up Picture**, controlling intensity and visibility through rendering. - New version removes smallest particle diameter limit in change-up pictures, allowing down to 0.01 (slow rendering) or 0.05 (balanced). - Save edited stickers to live material folder for reuse. --- ## Model Posture and Quality Adjustments - Change model posture to stature female model for better fitting demonstration. - Adjust clothing quality as needed. - Upgrade zippers to double-headed types in the attribute editor; this shows zippers with two heads pulling from middle, a common feature in bags and technical clothing.
